title: Rewiring the State — Eoin Mulgrew, No. 10 (Downing Street)
talk_summary: A recruitment/overview talk from the UK No.10 data science team about an 'insurgency model' of small elite teams of forward-deployed engineers embedded with policy/legal/ops teams to ship AI tools fast. It contains almost no technical mechanism detail, but a few organizational patterns (embedded FDEs, red-teaming before user rollout, in-house tooling over outsourcing, horizontal process automation) are loosely transferable.

takeaways.technique: Forward-deployed engineer embedding with the consuming team
takeaways.what_they_do: Engineers sit inside the team that will use the tool, observe their actual workflow and pain points, and co-design and ship in a couple of weeks rather than building from a spec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: first forward-deployed engineers ... embedding themselves with policy and operational teams ... observing their workflows, their pain points, co-designing solutions with them

takeaways.technique: Red-team models for sycophancy before putting in users' hands
takeaways.what_they_do: Before shipping a tool to non-expert users, they explicitly red-team the model for failure modes like sycophancy and coach users on the risks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's only because we have um sort of red team the models for that before we've put it into the hands of users

takeaways.technique: Build in-house instead of buying an outside analysis vendor
takeaways.what_they_do: Replaced a £1.5M external legal-analysis contract with one embedded engineer for a couple of weeks building a reusable internal tool the team can rerun on demand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were going to spend 1.5 million. Instead one of our engineers embedded with that team ... for a couple of weeks

takeaways.what_they_do: A tool that not only lets teams interrogate delivery reports but gives a second judgment on the reporting team — flagging known optimism bias, habitual amber ratings, and whether mitigations usually work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: does this department normally have a bit of optimism bias? ... are their mitigations usually effective or not?

takeaways.technique: Horizontal process automation over point solutions
takeaways.what_they_do: Moving from targeted one-off use cases to horizontal process work (transcription, call centers) that applies en masse across the system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would like to see us going after more of those like horizontal use cases that can be applied en masse across the system
